title: Preparation of Mollusc Larval Shells for Individual Geochemical Analysis
author: Vincent Mouchi
materials: Primar Plus TM – Trace analysis grade nitric acid (HNO3) (>68%)
On the next morning, transfer all materials from the PTFE beaker A to the PTFE beaker B (the one that contains the clean HNO 3 solution) for rinsing for 00:10:00 .
Transfer all materials from the PTFE beaker B (containing HNO 3 ) to the beaker A (now containing ultrapure water).
Leave 01:00:00 with Petri dish as cover.

steps.title: Prepare H2O2 Digestion Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a stabilized hydrogen peroxide solution to prevent shell dissolution during digestion.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL Suprapur® hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) 30% to a glass beaker.
Place the beaker on a magnetic stirrer and monitor pH.
Using a 1 mL cone with pipette, slowly add 0.15 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) until the pH reaches 8.5 (typically requires a volume of NaOH approximately equal to the initial H2O2 volume).
Activate the shaker and place the pH meter electrode in the solution to verify, then remove the electrode and deactivate the shaker.
Cover the beaker with parafilm and leave for at least 24h to allow gas release.
Note: This solution is active for approximately one week; prepare fresh every Monday for use Tuesday through Friday.

steps.title: Clean Labware and Tools
steps.instruction: Perform a rigorous acid-wash and ultrapure water rinse of all materials using PTFE beakers.

substeps.instruction: Fill two 2-L PTFE beakers (A and B) with 500 mL Primar Plus TM nitric acid (HNO3, >68%) each, then top up each with 1.5 L ultra-pure water (18.2 MΩcm).
Place Pasteur pipettes, Petri dishes, and zip plastic bags into beaker A.
Cover both beakers with PTFE lids and leave overnight under a fume hood.
Discard HNO3 from beaker A into a chemical waste container.
Rinse beaker A by adding 1 L ultrapure water and discarding; repeat this rinse twice more.
Fill beaker A with 2 L ultrapure water.
Transfer the HNO3 solution from beaker B to another beaker for storage (can be used as a first bath for other tools).
Rinse beaker B following the same procedure as beaker A (three 1 L ultrapure water rinses).
Place beaker A (containing water and materials) and beaker B (empty) overnight under a laminar flow cabinet with PTFE lids.
The following morning, add 2 L ultrapure water to beaker B.
Rinse each material from beaker A in the ultrapure water of beaker B for a few seconds, then place to dry under the laminar flow cabinet.
Dry Pasteur pipettes by shaking them by hand with a few strong strokes.
Place dried tools in cleaned, zipped plastic bags and store under the laminar flow cabinet.
Discard used ultrapure water from both beakers.

steps.title: Prepare Laboratory Environment
steps.instruction: Ensure a contaminant-free environment before starting sample preparation.

substeps.instruction: Activate the laminar flow cabinet and wait at least 1 hour before starting.
Wear a lab coat and nitrile gloves at all times.
Clean all laboratory surfaces and the inside of the laminar flow cabinet with low-lint wipes and absolute ethanol.
Clean glass salt dips with absolute ethanol using a squeeze bottle (no wipes) and let dry under the laminar flow cabinet.

steps.title: Process Larval Shells for Digestion
steps.instruction: Isolate larvae and treat them with H2O2 to remove organic matter.

substeps.instruction: Label glass salt dips with sample names using a permanent marker.
Thaw samples in microtubes for approximately 15 minutes.
Using an acid-washed Pasteur pipette, collect approximately 50 larvae and place them drop-by-drop onto the glass salt dip under a stereomicroscope to avoid sticking.
Ensure no larvae remain in the pipette (use ultrapure water to extract if necessary); discard the pipette.
Remove most of the collection water using a pipette with a low-retention tip, avoiding contact with the shells; discard the tip.
Slowly add 2 mL H2O2 to fill the glass salt dip, cover with a lid, and leave overnight.
Repeat this process for each sample (up to 200 specimens total).
Switch off the laminar flow cabinet overnight to prevent H2O2 evaporation.

steps.title: Verify and Complete Digestion
steps.instruction: Check for complete organic removal and refresh solution if necessary.

substeps.instruction: The following morning, verify digestion under a stereomicroscope: shells should be translucent under natural light and show a Maltese cross pattern under polarized light.
If digestion is incomplete, remove most of the solution with a low-retention tip, refill with 2 mL clean H2O2, and wait until complete. Discard the tip.
Once digestion is complete, remove most of the solution using a low-retention tip and discard the tip.
Fill the glass salt dip with ultrapure water using a pipette and low-retention tip; discard the tip.

steps.title: Mount Shells on Slides
steps.instruction: Transfer cleaned shells to adhesive tabs for geochemical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Clean a microscope slide with a low-lint wipe and absolute ethanol, apply an Extra Pure adhesive tab, and label the slide.
Clean a sable brush with absolute ethanol and re-hydrate it with ultrapure water.
Under a stereomicroscope (using polarized light), collect 1-5 larval shells at a time using the brush by capillarity.
Carefully place shells on the adhesive tab by slowly sweeping the brush across the surface under natural light.
Clean the brush with absolute ethanol and re-hydrate with ultrapure water between transfers.
Repeat until all specimens are transferred.
Allow the tab surface to dry under the laminar flow cabinet.
Circle the group of shells on the tab with a permanent marker.

steps.title: Final Cleanup and Storage
steps.instruction: Store samples and sanitize the workspace.

substeps.instruction: Clean the glass salt dip with ultrapure water and absolute ethanol, verify cleanliness under the stereomicroscope, and let dry under the laminar flow cabinet.
Store the slide in a clean slide box and seal the box with parafilm.
Wipe all room surfaces with low-lint wipes and absolute ethanol.
Switch off the laminar flow cabinet.
